nodes.label: Multi-select delivery options replace a single pickup/return location mode
Delivery fee pricing: per-location fee plus a flat area-radius fee
Rental snapshots which delivery option and which locations the customer chose

Rationale: legacy pickup_location_mode / return_location_mode values are backfilled into three boolean flags, so a tenant that used a mode on either the pickup or the return side keeps that option enabled
Per-plan dunning policy: grace period, max retry attempts and retry interval held in a JSONB config
Retry-eligibility selection: which failed installments may be charged again, and how soon
Operator choices: charge the first installment at checkout, and what portion of the cost gets split

Rationale: mark_installment_failed used to hardcode 3 retries and a 3-day grace period; it now reads the owning plan's config with those same numbers as COALESCE fallbacks so existing plans behave identically
Rationale: tenant installment_config is upgraded by JSONB merge guarded on NOT (config ? 'grace_period_days'), so operator-tuned settings survive and already-migrated tenants are skipped
Single-call customer 360 aggregate assembled for the Trax AI assistant
Rationale: no chat messages are stored server-side - conversation history is kept in client memory only
Gotcha: p_tenant_id is accepted but never used in any WHERE clause - every lookup filters on customer_id alone on the stated assumption that customer_id is globally unique
Gotcha: the aggregate selects FROM bonzah_policies while the insurance table defined in the schema is bonzah_insurance_policies
Legacy naming: agreements are surfaced to the assistant with a docusign_status field although e-signature runs on BoldSign
Customer-requested rental extension with a pending-approval state
Gotcha: previous_end_date holds the REQUESTED new end date while the request is pending and the ORIGINAL end date after approval - its meaning flips with is_extended
Chat delivery moves from a Socket.io server to the Supabase Realtime publication
Rationale: chat_channels is published alongside the message table so channel-level metadata such as last_message_at also propagates live
Rental renewal chain: a new rental links back to the rental it was renewed from
Row Level Security switched off on the rentals table
Blanket RLS disable looped over every table in the public schema
Consequence: tenant isolation stops being a database guarantee - existing policies remain defined but inert, so every query path must scope by tenant itself until RLS is re-enabled per table
Extension charges become a first-class ledger category
Pattern: adding one ledger category means dropping and recreating the whole CHECK with the complete list repeated, carrying forward legacy duplicates such as 'InitialFee' and 'Initial Fees'
The extension checkout URL is parked on the rental so a pending extension payment link can be re-shown or re-sent
Per-tenant subscription plan catalogue configured by the super admin
Plan rows mirror a Stripe Product/Price pair rather than pricing in-app
Read/write split: a tenant may SELECT its own plans, only service_role edge functions may mutate them
Configurable free-trial length per plan, with the real trial end mirrored back from Stripe
Platform-level billing: Drive247 charges each operator tenant a recurring fee, separate from the Stripe Connect flow used for booking payments
Invariant: at most one active, trialing or past_due subscription per tenant, enforced by a partial unique index
Stripe invoice history mirrored locally with hosted-invoice and PDF links
Design: tenants get SELECT only and every write goes through service_role, making the Stripe webhook the single source of truth for billing state
Card brand, last4 and expiry snapshotted on the subscription so the portal can render a payment method without calling Stripe
Rationale: update_updated_at_column() is created inside a DO block that swallows duplicate_function, so the migration is safe to run where the helper already exists
Gotcha: stripe_hosted_invoice_url and stripe_invoice_pdf act as bearer links that let any holder view and pay the invoice, so this table must never be pushed over a public broadcast channel
Auto go-live stamp recording when tenant onboarding setup completed
One-off data repair: dedupe agreement templates per tenant and template name
Rationale: duplicates were produced by race conditions in the template initialisation logic; a unique index on (tenant_id, template_name) makes the race harmless from now on
Every tenant is guaranteed one active template: 'Default Template' is preferred, otherwise the most recently updated row is activated
Optional free-text description shown with a pickup location
Self-service lockbox key handover instead of an in-person meet
Per-tenant lockbox master toggle, code length and notification channels
Lockbox combination and finding instructions stored on the vehicle row
Rental records how keys were actually handed over: lockbox, in_person, or NULL for a non-delivery rental
Per-tenant, per-channel lockbox notification templates with {{variable}} placeholders
Gotcha: the lockbox combination is stored as plain text on vehicles, a table whose RLS was switched off earlier in this schema history, so guarding it rests entirely on the application layer
Gotcha: the FOR ALL policy on lockbox_templates tests only tenant membership, so any authenticated user of the tenant - viewer and ops included - can rewrite the templates that carry lockbox codes
Lockbox code length relaxed from a fixed 4/6/8 choice to any length between 1 and 20
Operator's preferred display unit (hours or days) for booking lead time
Rationale: the lead time is always stored in hours in booking_lead_time_hours; this column only records how the admin UI should present it
Excess mileage charging: a per-mile rate applied once a rental passes the vehicle's included mileage
Convention: allowed_mileage NULL means unlimited included mileage, so no excess is ever charged
Granular per-tab access control - the manager is the only role whose access is not a fixed level
Two access levels per granted tab: viewer (read-only) or editor
Three stacked SELECT policies: a user reads their own grants, a head_admin reads their tenant's users' grants, a super admin reads all
Design: only service_role may INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, so grants can only change through an edge function and never straight from the portal client
Gotcha: the table carries no tenant_id - tenant scoping exists only through the join to app_users, so every cross-tenant guarantee depends on that join
'manager' added to the app_users role vocabulary
Stub: invoice breakdown columns were applied straight to the remote database, no DDL is committed
Pattern and gotcha: some schema changes are applied directly to the remote database with only a stub file committed, so the migrations directory is not a complete description of the live schema
Stub: the excess-mileage charge category was applied straight to the remote database
Stub: customer address fields were applied straight to the remote database

hyperedges.label: Rental extension flow: pending request, payment link, ledger category and the dates that flip meaning
Platform subscription billing schema: per-tenant plan catalogue, Stripe price mirror, trials, the single-live-subscription invariant and webhook-only writes
RLS turned off across the whole schema, then reintroduced table by table on each new table created afterwards
